key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical ensemble using QSVM and VQC can improve phishing detection in Ethereum transaction networks, with QSVM showing the strongest anomaly-detection behavior.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests QML could become a useful component for fraud and anomaly detection pipelines when paired with classical models and efficient feature encoding.
method: Train QSVM and VQC on real Ethereum transaction data
Compare QRAC-based encodings against the ZZ feature map
Evaluate on simulators and the IBM Heron quantum processor
evidence_signal: QRAC improved performance over ZZ by about 13% for VQC and 3% for QSVM, and QSVM consistently produced the lowest false negatives and higher recall.
watch_item: Current QML gains still do not surpass leading deep learning methods, and hardware performance remains dependent on quantum device quality and volume.
paper_title: Detecting Phishing in Ethereum Networks using Quantum Machine Learning
